figures.method: For each figure, run the tool in the CHART_FONT_BROKEN=1 arm and diff it against the published PNG pixel by pixel. If the broken arm reproduces the archive, the ONLY thing that changed is the font and the figure is safe to redraw. If it does not, the data has moved and it is not mine to restate. This is the predecessor's method and the brief's instruction.

left_alone.docs/shots/2026-08-08-w1-01-r4-the-road-: ITS DATA HAS MOVED AND I DID NOT RESTATE IT. The broken arm differs from the archive by 5,148 pixels across the whole plot, not just the text. Cause found and proven, not guessed: the figure was committed at c36653e, and W1-ROAD-JOIN then rerouted game/data/world/roads.json (commit 6c54c3b), taking the crossing from 6816 m to 6911.4 m. Proof: rebuilt in an out-of-repo sandbox with roads.json rolled back to c36653e, and the broken arm then reproduces the archive except for the 7-glyph commit stamp. So roads.json is the ONLY input that moved, and the figure now on disk is a picture of W1-01-r4's finding in a world that no longer exists. Redrawing it at HEAD would publish W1-ROAD-JOIN's post-join world under W1-01-r4's headline; publishing the sandbox reconstruction would stamp a commit whose roads.json did not draw it, and would not be reproducible from the tree by anyone else. Both are a false finding of a different kind, so the original stands and W1-01-r4 owns the redraw. Its tool is now clean, so that redraw is one command.

the_gate.scope: the STAGED BLOBS of the commit, via a new `node tools/lib/chart-font.mjs --audit-staged`. NOT the whole tree, and the deviation is deliberate: a whole-tree hard gate deadlocks every agent on the box over a neighbour's uncommitted scratch file, which is the exact failure rule 13 exists to prevent. Staged scope still catches the only way the defect actually spreads — a paste reaching a commit — including through tools/bank.mjs's `git add -A`. The tree-wide sweep still runs afterwards as a warning so drift stays visible.
the_gate.rule_13: The tree was silent BEFORE the gate was armed, and provably so: `--audit-tree` exits 0 naming nothing, and the five wiring edits are already in HEAD (banked at a2031bb) while the armed hook is in this commit. The assertion cannot land ahead of the data it demands.
the_gate.one_definition: the regex for a sheared literal now lives once, in chart-font.mjs, shared by --audit-tree, --audit-staged and --audit-selftest. A second copy of it in the hook would have been this piece's own mistake repeated.
the_gate.watched_going_red: end-to-end in a throwaway git repo (never the shared index), with the real hook script and the real tool: (1) a chart tool carrying the sheared table, staged -> BLOCKED, commit refused, nothing landed; (2) the same tool wired to the shared module -> passes, commit lands; (3) `git add -A` with a sheared file present, i.e. the bank's own route -> BLOCKED. Plus `--audit-selftest`, which requires the detector to trip on the archived pre-fix table and stay silent on the fixed one.

self_test.result: PASS, both halves. The shipped table renders '28 OF 32' and 'BOOK' correctly against hand-written expected pixels; the SAME assertions run against the archived pre-fix table produce exactly 62 failures — 53 glyphs of the wrong width, 4 bad rows in '28 OF 32', 5 bad rows in 'BOOK' — which is the figure the predecessor recorded, unchanged. The control fails on digits AND on letters, and the self-test fails itself if that control ever comes back clean.
self_test.also_still_green: --provenance (36 restored / 17 re-authored, no drift warning; the count moved 35->36 and 52->53 glyphs only because I did not change the table — see not_done).

the_sweep.why: The predecessor's damage list came from tool output paths and owners' status files and said so: it never looked at the images. This looks at the images.
the_sweep.tool: tools/analysis/w1-chartfont-shot-sweep.mjs — decodes every PNG in docs/shots/ (all five PNG filters, colour type 2 and 6) and asks the pixels which glyph table drew them.
the_sweep.it_can_fail: --self-test renders a known string through each table and requires the classifier to name the right one, and a flat image to be classified as neither.
the_sweep.the_first_version_was_worthless_and_that: counting every matching 5x5 block passed the self-test and then called all four KNOWN-SHEARED figures 'sound', because axis rules and bar edges produce tens of thousands of accidental punctuation matches (46,539 on one figure) that swamp ~700 real glyphs. Fixed by counting only alphanumerics inside runs of >=3 glyph cells sharing one baseline, one ink colour and one paper colour, and by deciding on the sheared RATIO rather than raw counts — because a sheared glyph often equals some OTHER sound glyph, which is the defect itself. Calibrated against eight images with known labels: sheared 0.91-1.00, sound 0.00.

result.headline: IT FOUND NOTHING THE PROVENANCE LIST HAD MISSED. Every figure it names was already named in reports/w1-chartfont-damage.md, and the three I regenerated now read 'sound' with zero sheared hits. The predecessor flagged its own list as possibly incomplete because it had never looked at the images; the images say it was complete. That converts 'we think we found them all' into a measurement.

result.one_false_positive_found_and_fixed_rathe: An earlier cut also flagged docs/shots/2026-08-08-w1-dlg-s37-the-reader-stopped-scoring.png at ratio 0.10. It is NOT sheared — it is drawn in this project's other font, a genuine 5x7 at 35 chars, and sampling a 5x7 glyph through a 5x5 window throws off junk matches in both tables. The tell was in the data: all 47 of its sheared hits were TWO shapes ('7' and 'A') repeated, while every genuinely sheared figure shows 27-30 DISTINCT sheared glyphs because a real caption uses the whole alphabet. The verdict rule now requires a broad alphabet as well as a high ratio. I checked that 5x7 font's table directly before concluding: 46 glyphs, every one exactly 35 characters, no defect.

the_sweep.performance_note: The first working version was correct but spent all its time in the garbage collector — a 25-character string plus a 25-element array allocated per pixel per scale, ~9M allocations per image, and 164 images had not finished in ten minutes. Rewritten to compare 25-bit integers against a packed Int32Array. Same algorithm; equivalence checked by reproducing the string version's counts EXACTLY on seven known-label images (656/6, 840/36, 1147/111, 578/0, 662, 876, 1258). 3m23s for the whole directory.

It is unchanged behaviour, not a regression — the other four never had it either. I could restore it provably (the pre-fix string reduces to a clean two-character deletion), but adding a glyph means adding it to SHEARED_FONT too, and that changes what the CHART_FONT_BROKEN arm draws — which would invalidate the byte-identity delete-the-fix evidence the predecessor's rule-6 result rests on. Not worth a cosmetic gain. Named here so the next author decides deliberately.
